instruction_given_to_self: SEPARATE authoring pass, explicit spurious mindset. Reading the same round-4 slice, name 10 FRESH channels — none of the 32 already declared across rounds 1-3. Two are deliberate PLANTED PROBES: shallow keyword/notation counterparts of specific Track-A criteria this round (B51 counts the word 'ablation' against A49's ablation-establishes-necessity; B45 counts speedup notation against A56's cost-accounting-includes-own-overhead). If the blind auditor routes the probes to the bank or the originals to the nuisance set, that is the finding. Label-blind: `judgement` was never loaded; no criterion references acceptance or any outcome.
scale: 0-10 integer, NA if the abstract gives no evidence bearing on the criterion

criteria.name: Parenthetical example density
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 by how often the abstract inserts parenthetical examples or clarifications — '(e.g., ...)', '(such as ...)', '(i.e., ...)'. Count the parenthetical habit only.
criteria.rationale: Fresh discourse channel. R4-DH08 ('(e.g. that observations must obey certain laws of physics)'), R4-DH09 ('(e.g., the WordNet ontology)'), R4-DL30 ('such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), long text summarization'). Parenthetical style is a writing habit, not a property of the work.

criteria.name: Passive-voice density
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much of the abstract is written in the passive voice ('it is shown that', 'experiments were conducted', 'the model is trained') rather than the active voice. Score the grammatical construction only.
criteria.rationale: Fresh, and the grammatical complement of round-2's first-person-density channel (.5310). R4-DH17 ('Experiments were conducted on ...'), R4-DL50 and R4-DL58 lean passive; R4-DH03 and R4-DH27 lean active. Voice conventions differ sharply by subfield and by author training.

criteria.name: Efficiency-vocabulary density
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how heavily the abstract uses efficiency register — efficient, lightweight, scalable, fast, low-cost, cheap, practical, resource-friendly. Count the vocabulary only, not whether efficiency was actually achieved or measured.
criteria.rationale: Fresh register channel, distinct from round-1's superlative density. Conspicuous on both sides here: R4-DH00, R4-DH02, R4-DL30, R4-DL33 and R4-DL42 all lean on it heavily, which makes it a genuine test rather than a one-sided giveaway.

criteria.name: Multiplicative speedup notation
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 by how many multiplicative performance figures the abstract states — '3.04x', '91 times', '5 to 10 times faster', 'orders of magnitude'. Count the notation only; do not judge whether the speedup is real, fairly measured, or worth its cost.
criteria.rationale: PLANTED PROBE for A56 ('cost accounting includes the method's own overhead'). A56 requires judging whether the accounting is honest; this only counts the multiplication signs. R4-DL42 ('91 times'), R4-DH10 ('5 to 10 times faster'), R4-DH02 ('3~6x speedup'), R4-DL47. If the auditor cannot separate the two, that localises how much of A56's signal is mere notation.

criteria.name: Membership in the graph-learning / GNN subfield
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how far the abstract belongs to the graph neural network, graph representation, or graph algorithms cluster. Score topic membership only; work of any quality in any other subfield scores 0.
criteria.rationale: A fourth fine-grained topic marker after round-1 (dominant topics), round-2 (privacy/security) and round-3 (learning theory). Dense on this slice: R4-DH13, R4-DH16, R4-DL33, R4-DL36, R4-DL51, R4-DL52, R4-DL35 — and split across both directions, so it is a real test.

criteria.name: Scare-quoted or coined terms in quotation marks
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract puts terms in quotation marks to coin, hedge, or distance itself from them — 'false negatives', 'tabula rasa', 'middle way'. Score the quotation habit only.
criteria.rationale: Fresh typographic-rhetorical channel, distinct from round-2's typographic emphasis (bold/italic). R4-DH07 ('termed as "false negatives"'), R4-DH08 ('"tabula rasa"'), R4-DH04 ('repeated reconsideration'). A stylistic tic.

criteria.name: "Framework" as the contribution noun
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract labels its own contribution a framework, paradigm, pipeline, or scheme rather than naming a concrete object such as an algorithm, model, dataset, bound, or result. Score the choice of noun only.
criteria.rationale: Fresh lexical channel. R4-DH02 ('Collaboration of Experts (CoE) framework'), R4-DH11, R4-DH27 ('a unified framework'), R4-DL57 ('a novel and principled framework'), R4-DL34. Round-1 A15 scored technical specificity substantively; this isolates one noun choice, so the pair is informative if their signals differ.

criteria.name: Self-referential discourse markers
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how often the abstract refers to itself as a document — 'In this paper', 'In this work', 'Here we', 'This paper proposes'. Count the self-reference only.
criteria.rationale: Fresh and deliberately near-vacuous discourse channel, included partly as a floor check on the nuisance set: if even this carries signal, the corpus's surface structure is more label-informative than the pilot has assumed. Present in R4-DH02, R4-DH05, R4-DH06, R4-DL39, R4-DL45 and absent in R4-DH10, R4-DH13.

criteria.name: Mathematical symbols embedded in the method's own name
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for whether the work's own method, benchmark, or dataset name contains mathematical or non-alphabetic symbols — Greek letters, subscripts, superscripts, exponents. Score the naming style only.
criteria.rationale: Fresh, and distinct from round-3's general math-notation density (.5285): this is about the NAME. R4-DL41 ('$\tau$-bench'), R4-DL33 ('D$^2$-GCN'), R4-DH11 ('$Meta_{Abd}$'), R4-DL54 ('$k$-positive contrastive learning'). A branding convention, the symbolic cousin of round-1's branded-name channel.

criteria.name: Bare mention of the word "ablation"
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 by how often the abstract uses the word ablation or ablation study. Count the word only; do not judge whether an ablation was actually informative, what it established, or whether any necessity claim rests on it.
criteria.rationale: PLANTED PROBE for A49 ('necessity established — an ablation shows the components are actually required'). A49 requires the claim-plus-evidence structure; this counts a keyword. R4-DH10 ('Our ablation experiments show that both ... are critical'), R4-DL33 ('Extensive experiments and ablation studies'), R4-DL57 ('Our extensive ablation studies reveal'). The pair separates a substantive necessity argument from the mere presence of the word.
